nodes.name: Reindeer lichen
nodes.desc: A pale lichen carpeting the woodland floor. Wikipedia calls lichens a staple for caribou in winter, which dig through snow to reach them.

nodes.name: Willows
nodes.desc: Shrubby willows grow along the Kobuk and on the tundra edge. Moose browse their shoots and caribou also feed on them.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Grass-like plants of wet tundra and river flats, among the most recorded plants near the park.

nodes.name: Arctic grasses
nodes.desc: Hardy grasses of dry slopes and gravel. GloBI records common redpolls eating Poa glauca.

nodes.name: Caribou
nodes.desc: Around 400,000 caribou of the Western Arctic herd cross the Kobuk River each year between winter and calving grounds. They feed on lichen in winter.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: Browses willow shoots and twigs in winter and eats forbs and aquatic plants in summer. Wolves, bears and wolverines all use it.

nodes.name: Tundra vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of damp tundra and river flats, and a staple prey of foxes, wolves and bears in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Brown lemming
nodes.desc: A tundra rodent that eats sedges and other low plants. Lemmings undergo large swings in numbers, which ripple up to their predators.

nodes.name: Northern red-backed vole
nodes.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. A small woodland vole eating seeds, berries, fungi and lichen, and preyed on by foxes and wolverines.

nodes.name: Common redpoll
nodes.desc: A small finch that eats seeds and shoots. GloBI records it eating grasses and horsetail.

nodes.name: Wolverine
nodes.desc: Mainly a scavenger that relies on carrion, often from wolf kills, but also hunts small mammals and sometimes weakened large animals.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Listed by the park service among its predators. A small hunter of voles and lemmings.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A year-round scavenger that feeds on carrion at carcasses left by larger predators.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Wolf packs hunt caribou and moose in the park, and their kills feed wolverines, ravens and bears.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that takes moose calves and small rodents, and often scavenges wolf kills.

nodes.name: Summer light
nodes.desc: The park lies north of the Arctic Circle, so growth is crammed into a short summer of very long days.

nodes.name: Snow cover
nodes.desc: Long winters bury willow and lichen under snow, forcing caribou to dig for food. Meltwater feeds tundra plants in spring.

nodes.name: Kobuk River
nodes.desc: The river divides the park. Caribou cross it each year, and its valley is a wetland that supports willows and sedges.

nodes.name: Thin cold soil
nodes.desc: Plants face strong winds, thin soils and a short growing season, according to the park service.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Slowly break down dead plants and carcasses in the cold soil and return nutrients to it.
